text: Ask your doctor or pharmacist how long to take it before you start.
A herbal tea can replace your maintenance meds.
Do not stop or change maintenance medicines without talking to your doctor.
Taking pills every day is tiring and costly. A natural tea that promises freedom from pills sounds like a gift.
Bring the tea and your questions to your doctor or barangay health center before changing anything.
CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: do not stop maintenance medicines without your doctor
If it is natural, it is always safe.
Natural does not mean safe. Some herbs can harm you or clash with medicines.
Plants from the garden feel gentle and familiar, and our elders used them. Factory pills feel strong and strange.
Tell your health worker about every herb or supplement you take, together with your medicines.
WHO traditional medicine guidance; CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts
A food supplement can cure your illness.
Supplements are not medicine. In the Philippines their labels must say "No approved therapeutic claims".
Supplement ads look like medicine ads, with doctors, charts and happy families. It is hard to tell them apart.
Read the label for "No approved therapeutic claims" and check the FDA Philippines verification portal.
FDA Philippines rules on food supplement labelling
An FDA number means it cures whatever the ad says.
Registration is not proof of every claim. Health claims on supplements are a red flag.
An official-looking number feels like a stamp of approval for the whole ad, not just the product.
Look up the product on the FDA Philippines portal and compare what it is registered as.
FDA Philippines verification portal; food supplement labelling rules
Vaccines are never checked after they come out.
Vaccines are tested in large studies and monitored after approval. Side effects are reported and reviewed.
We rarely see the safety work, so it is easy to think nobody is watching. Worry about our children is natural.
Ask your health worker how side effects are reported. Look at DOH vaccine pages.
WHO vaccine safety monitoring; CONTENT_GUIDE vaccine framing
A fever after a vaccine means it is dangerous.
Most side effects are mild and short, like a sore arm or mild fever. Serious ones are rare.
Seeing your child feverish is scary, and scary stories get shared more than calm ones.
Ask the health center what reactions are normal and which signs mean you should come back.
WHO vaccine safety Q&A; CONTENT_GUIDE vaccine framing
Good vaccines are only for people who can pay.
Routine childhood vaccines are available free at health centers.
Many things that matter cost money, so free can feel like second-best. Not everyone hears about free programs.
Visit or call your barangay health center and ask for the childhood vaccine schedule.
DOH national immunization program
Sharing every vaccine warning keeps my family safe.
Fear spreads faster than facts. Checking with a health worker first is a caring habit.
Forwarding a warning feels like protecting the people we love. Nobody wants to be the one who stayed quiet.
Pause before sharing. Ask a health worker or check an independent fact-checker first.
CONTENT_GUIDE vaccine framing: fear spreads faster than facts
You will feel it if your blood pressure is high.
High blood pressure often has no symptoms. Regular checks at the health center help.
Some people do get headaches, so it makes sense to wait for a sign. Feeling fine feels like being fine.
Get your blood pressure checked at the barangay health center, even when you feel well.
Ampalaya tea cures diabetes.
Ampalaya is a healthy vegetable, but there is no proven herbal cure for diabetes.
Ampalaya is bitter and good for us, and many grandparents swear by it. It feels like strong medicine.
Keep your prescribed medicine and ask your doctor before adding any herbal product.
CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: no proven herbal cure for diabetes
A secret herbal mix cures cancer, but doctors hide it.
There is no proven herbal cure for cancer. Early check-ups and screening help.
Cancer is frightening and treatment is hard. A gentle secret cure gives hope when we need it most.
Ask where the evidence is. Bring the claim to a doctor and check an independent fact-checker.
WHO cancer fact sheet; CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts
Once my BP is normal, I can stop my maintenance meds.
A normal reading often means the medicine is working. Ask your doctor before any change.
A good reading feels like being cured. It is natural to hope the pills are no longer needed.
Bring your readings to your doctor and ask what they mean for your medicine.
Washing hands after hard work causes pasma, a hand ailment.
Washing with soap and water helps prevent infections. If hand pain or shaking continues, see a health worker.
Pasma is a folk belief our elders passed down to protect us. Tired, aching hands after work are real, and the warning comes from care.
Keep washing with soap and water. Ask your health worker about hand pain that does not go away.
WHO hand hygiene guidance; respectful handling of pasma per CONTENT_GUIDE
A cough that lasts for weeks is just a normal cough.
A cough of 2 weeks or more should be checked for TB. TB is curable, with free treatment.
Coughs are common, and nobody wants to bother the health center for "just a cough".
Go to the barangay health center and ask for a TB check if a cough lasts 2 weeks.
WHO tuberculosis fact sheet; DOH TB program
A home remedy is enough for a small dog bite.
Wash the wound with soap and running water, then go to an animal bite center right away.
Small bites look harmless, and traditional healers are close and trusted. The pet may be family too.
Go to the nearest animal bite center the same day. Rabies is preventable but deadly once symptoms start.
WHO rabies fact sheet; DOH animal bite centers
Flood water is harmless if you feel fine after.
Wading in flood water raises leptospirosis risk. See a health worker after exposure.
During floods we wade because we must. Feeling fine the next day makes it seem like nothing happened.
Tell your health worker you waded in flood water, even if you feel fine.
WHO leptospirosis guidance; DOH flood advisories
Drink less during diarrhea so it stops sooner.
ORS helps prevent dehydration from diarrhea. See a health worker for danger signs.
Less going in seems like less coming out. It is a logical guess when you are tired and worried.
WHO diarrhoeal disease fact sheet (ORS)
If water looks clear, it is safe to drink.
Clear water can still carry germs. Bringing it to a rolling boil makes it safer.
We judge with our eyes, and clean-looking water from a familiar source feels safe.
Ask your barangay health worker if your water source is safe, or boil it when unsure.
WHO drinking-water guidance
Vaping is harmless because it is just water vapour.
Smoking and vaping both harm the lungs and heart.
Vapes smell sweet and look like a clean mist, and they are often sold as the safer choice.
Ask your health worker about vaping, or look at DOH pages on tobacco and vapes.
WHO tobacco and e-cigarette fact sheets
Teens are young and strong, so they need less sleep.
Teens need more sleep than adults. Sleep supports mood, memory and the immune system.
Teens seem full of energy late at night, and adults remember pulling all-nighters too.
Ask a health worker or school nurse how much sleep a teen needs.
WHO adolescent health guidance; sleep and wellbeing consensus
If a message was forwarded many times, it must be true.
Many shares do not make a claim true. Check the source before you forward.
When many people we trust share something, it feels checked already. Sharing is how we care for each other.
Find who first said it. Look for a second trusted source, like DOH or a fact-checker.
Media literacy consensus; independent fact-checking practice
A chatbot always tells the truth.
Chatbots can sound sure and still be wrong. Check health answers with a health worker.
Chatbots answer fast, in neat sentences, with a confident tone. That sounds like an expert.
Ask the same question to a health worker, or check a DOH or WHO page.
CONTENT_GUIDE AI facts: AI can be confidently wrong (hallucination)
A health chatbot can diagnose me like a doctor.
Chatbots cannot examine you and are not doctors. They can help you prepare questions.
Clinics can be far and busy, and the chatbot is always awake. It feels like a doctor in your pocket.
Use the chatbot to write your questions, then bring them to a health worker. Skip your full name and ID numbers.
CONTENT_GUIDE AI facts: chatbots are not doctors
If a doctor is in the video ad, the product works.
Doctor videos can be faked with AI. A real doctor selling a miracle product is a red flag.
We were taught to respect doctors. A familiar white coat and a calm voice feel trustworthy.
Look for the doctor's own official page and the product's FDA registration.
CONTENT_GUIDE AI facts: deepfaked doctor endorsements
You can always spot a fake video by its glitches.
AI fakes can look and sound real. Checking the source works better than hunting glitches.
Early fakes had odd blinking and blurry mouths, and tips for spotting them went viral.
Ask who posted it first, and look for the same news on an official page.
CONTENT_GUIDE AI facts: spotting glitches is unreliable
If "they" deleted the post, it must be true.
Posts are removed for many reasons, including false health claims. Removal is not proof.
Being told something is hidden makes it feel precious. Nobody likes the feeling of being kept in the dark.
Search an independent fact-checker for the claim before you repost it.
Platform policies on health misinformation; fact-checking practice
An "AI-powered" health product must be smarter and safer.
"AI-powered" is often just a sales label. Ask what it does and whether it is proven.
AI is in the news every day, so the word sounds modern and impressive.
Ask the seller what the AI actually does, and check the product with the FDA portal.
Module 1 lesson on AI hype; FDA Philippines verification portal
My phone shows tea ads because it secretly listens to me.
Apps learn patterns from what you tap, watch and search, then guess what to show you.
The ads can feel spookily on point, right after we talked about something. Of course it feels like listening.
Open the app's ad settings to see why an ad was shown, and review app permissions.
Module 1 lesson: AI learns patterns from examples to make guesses
I already had dengue, so I cannot get it again.
There are four types of dengue virus. A second infection can be more severe, so stay careful.
After a hard bout of dengue, it feels fair to think the body is now protected. Some illnesses, like chickenpox, usually come only once.
Keep up the 4S at home. If a fever comes back, see a health worker early and mention your past dengue.
WHO fact sheet: Dengue and severe dengue (2025): a second infection raises the risk of severe dengue
Once the fever breaks, dengue is over.
Severe dengue signs often appear after the fever goes away. Keep watching for warning signs.
A falling fever is usually the best news a family can get. After days of worry, everyone is ready to rest.
Ask your health worker which warning signs to watch for. Go to the hospital at once if any appear.
WHO fact sheet: Dengue and severe dengue (2025): severe symptoms often come after the fever has gone
Any pain reliever at home is fine for a dengue fever.
Some common pain relievers can raise bleeding risk in dengue. Ask a health worker before taking any.
